entities.name: Eye of Ra
entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
The Eye of Ra, a potent symbol originating in ancient Egyptian mythology, embodies protection, royal power, and fertility. It is often associated with the sun god Ra, one of the most significant deities in the Egyptian pantheon, who ruled over the sky and the underworld. This emblem, also known as the 'Eye of Horus' or 'Wadjet' in some contexts, illustrates the intertwining of religion and politics in ancient Egypt, which lasted from approximately 3100 BCE until the conquest by Alexander the Great in 332 BCE. The Eye of Ra's imagery adorned temples, tombs, and amulets, signifying its importance in both the afterlife and daily life of the Egyptian people.

The Eye of Ra played a crucial role in various aspects of ancient Egyptian life, including funerary practices, where it was believed to provide protection against evil and ensure safe passage to the afterlife. Pharaohs, such as Ramses II and Tutankhamun, utilized the symbol to legitimize their reigns and invoke divine support, further embedding the Eye into the fabric of Egyptian culture and governance. Artistic depictions often portrayed the Eye as a stylized representation, incorporating elements of the falcon, symbolizing Ra’s power and omnipresence.

The legacy of the Eye of Ra extends beyond ancient Egypt, influencing various cultures and religious beliefs throughout history. Its iconography has permeated into modern art and literature, where it is frequently invoked as a symbol of protection and insight. The Eye’s association with the sun and vision has led to its adoption in various esoteric traditions and contemporary spiritual movements, showcasing its enduring significance.
